note: Research output used to build js/checklists.js. final = reconciled checklist per item type (with reasoning per checkpoint); citationAudit = adversarial citation audit of the draft; fieldReview = senior field-QC review of the draft.

checks.text: Previous punch/NCR items closed, verified
checks.unknownQuestion: Where is the current punch/NCR list for this line, and who signs closure?
checks.reasoning: Checking closures is most of the work at this stage. QC must see the fix on the pipe, not only the signature.

checks.text: Leak test done, record signed
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 para 137 (Pressure Tests) or ASME B31.3 para 345 (Testing; 345.3.1 joints exposed during leak test), per project line class (confirm project edition)
defects: Line not in a test boundary
checks.unknownQuestion: Which test type and limit cover this line (hydro/pneumatic/initial service), and is it released?
checks.reasoning: Both codes require a leak test before service and allow alternatives to hydro, so the accepted test type is unknown. Welding visible after the test is a common violation.

checks.text: Weld/NDE records complete, no open repairs
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 para 136 (Inspection and Examination) or ASME B31.3 para 341 (Examination), per project line class; NDE methods per ASME Sec V; welder/procedure qualification per ASME Sec IX; PWHT and welder ID traceability: verify clause/edition (confirm project edition)
checks.unknownQuestion: What NDE extent and PWHT (if any) apply to this line class, and is PMI required for this material?
checks.reasoning: The code requires examination, but its extent, PWHT and PMI depend on line class and project spec. At this stage it is a record check only.

checks.text: Routing and inline items as drawn
checks.unknownQuestion: Are field changes red-lined and approved, and is an inline-item list per line available?
checks.reasoning: Undocumented field changes affect stress analysis and as-builts. Reversed check valves, strainers or traps are common. Skip the inline items if a separate valve checklist covers them.

checks.text: Clear of steel/cables; sleeves sealed
checks.unknownQuestion: What minimum clearances and walkway headroom apply, and which penetrations need fire-stop or watertight seals?
checks.reasoning: Contact causes wear and corrosion and restrains movement. Open wall or bund penetrations are easy to see. All clearance and seal values are project-defined, so unknown.

checks.text: Pipe surface undamaged, temp lugs removed
checks.unknownQuestion: What acceptance limits apply to dents, gouges and arc strikes, and what examination is needed after temp lug removal?
checks.reasoning: Late damage comes from scaffolding, lifting and nearby grinding. Non-metallic and lined pipe have their own visible defects. Acceptance limits are unknown.

checks.text: All supports installed, type as drawn
defects: SS pipe on bare CS support
checks.unknownQuestion: Is the support drawing set on site the latest revision, and is an isolation pad required between SS pipe and CS supports?
checks.reasoning: Support type and location come from the stress/support design. Over-tight clamps block sliding lines or point-load plastic pipe.

checks.text: No temporary supports or wedges left
checks.unknownQuestion: Were temporary supports added for hydrotest, and are they listed?
checks.reasoning: Leftover temporary restraints change load paths and block thermal growth. Hydrotest supports on gas/air lines are easy to miss.

checks.text: Shoes seated, guides/slides free
checks.unknownQuestion: Which supports are anchors or guides, and what gaps and shoe overhang are specified?
checks.reasoning: A support only works if the pipe bears on it and can move as designed. Gap and overhang values are project-defined.

checks.text: Spring hangers: stops/setting per plan
checks.unknownQuestion: When are travel stops removed (after test or before hot commissioning), and by whom? Cold settings and rod-angle limits are vendor/project values.
checks.reasoning: Stops may stay in on purpose until hot commissioning, so judge against the plan, not a blanket rule. Mark N/A if the line has no spring hangers.

checks.text: Expansion joints: bars/rods per vendor
checks.unknownQuestion: When are shipping bars removed, and what limit-rod settings does the vendor give?
checks.reasoning: Shipping bars left in, wrong rod settings and reversed liners are common handover punch items. Settings are vendor values. Mark N/A if there are none.

checks.text: Small-bore branches braced/supported
checks.unknownQuestion: Does the project spec require bracing on small-bore branches, and are threaded joints to be seal-welded?
checks.reasoning: Unbraced vents, drains and instrument branches are a known cause of vibration fatigue, especially near pumps. Vibration cannot be seen before start-up.

checks.text: Slope per design, drains/vents per spec
checks.unknownQuestion: Which lines must slope and at what slope, and which end closure (plug/cap/blind) and single or double valve are required?
checks.reasoning: A designed pocket is acceptable if it is drained, and liquid-full lines may need no slope. Drain/vent locations and closures come from the P&ID and spec.

checks.text: Blinds per status list, temp items gone
checks.unknownQuestion: Is there a blind/spectacle status list for handover, and who maintains it?
checks.reasoning: Boundary blinds may stay in by design at handover. A test blind left in, or a missing boundary isolation, is a start-up safety risk.

checks.text: Items removed for test reinstated
checks.unknownQuestion: Who signs reinstatement (construction, QC or commissioning), and which items stay out until flushing ends?
checks.reasoning: Spools, PSVs, instruments and orifice plates are removed for test or flushing. Re-made joints need a new gasket and recorded torque.

checks.text: Flushed and drained, open ends sealed
checks.unknownQuestion: Is flushing in construction or commissioning scope, and what preservation applies after test (drain, dry, N2, inhibitor)?
checks.reasoning: Debris damages pumps and valves, and test water left in SS demin or gas/air lines causes corrosion. Scope and acceptance are project-defined.

checks.text: Paint complete, damage touched up
checks.unknownQuestion: What coating system, colour and DFT apply to this line?
checks.reasoning: Coating system and DFT are spec values that can't be confirmed by eye. Defects show at field welds, supports and grade entries. Mark N/A for unpainted SS or non-metallic pipe.

checks.text: Insulation/cladding complete, sealed
checks.unknownQuestion: What insulation type and thickness apply, and which lines need personnel protection?
checks.reasoning: Unsealed or wrongly lapped cladding lets water in (corrosion under insulation). Scope and type are project-defined. Mark N/A if the line is not insulated.

checks.text: Line ID and flow arrows fitted
checks.unknownQuestion: What is the project marking standard (colours, spacing, locations)?
checks.reasoning: Correct identification is needed for safe isolation and commissioning. The marking standard is set by the project.

checks.text: Spray shields/bonding jumpers fitted
checks.unknownQuestion: Which chemical lines need flange spray shields, and which lines need bonding jumpers or insulating joints?
checks.reasoning: A missing shield on an acid/caustic flange may justify Category A. Bonding matters on fuel gas. Mark N/A where neither applies.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 345 (345.3.1 joints exposed); ASME B31.1 para 137 (confirm project edition)
citationAudit.correctedRef: ASME B31.1 para 137 (Pressure Tests) or ASME B31.3 para 345 (Testing; 345.3.1 joints exposed during leak test), per project line class (confirm project edition)
citationAudit.evidence: The numbers and content are right. B31.3 Chapter VI para 345 is 'Testing', and 345.3.1 requires joints, welds and bonds to be left uninsulated and exposed during the leak test, except joints already tested under B31.3 (secondary sources safteng.net and whatispiping.com quote this). The para 345 numbering is stable across the 2016 to 2022 editions as far as I know. B31.1 para 137 is 'Pressure Tests' in Chapter VI. B31.1 has a similar joint-exposure rule, but I could not confirm its sub-paragraph number, so don't add a B31.1 sub-number. The only fix is wording: the ref lists both codes together, as if both apply to every line. Which code governs which BOP system is a project question, so phrase it as 'B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class'.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 341; ASME B31.1 para 136; NDE methods per ASME Sec V; welder quals per ASME Sec IX (confirm project edition)
citationAudit.correctedRef: ASME B31.1 para 136 (Inspection and Examination) or ASME B31.3 para 341 (Examination), per project line class; NDE methods per ASME Sec V; welder/procedure qualification per ASME Sec IX; PWHT and welder ID traceability: verify clause/edition (confirm project edition)
citationAudit.evidence: B31.3 para 341 is 'Examination' (Chapter VI: 340 Inspection, 341 Examination, 342 Personnel, 343 Procedures, 344 Types, 345 Testing, 346 Records). B31.1 para 136 is 'Inspection and Examination'. I'm confident of both numbers and titles. Citing Sec V and Sec IX without a clause is fine. Two problems: (1) as with the leak-test ref, both codes are listed together, so reword to 'per project line class'; (2) the defects 'PWHT record missing' and 'Welder ID not traceable' are not covered by 341/136. PWHT is in the separate heat-treatment paragraphs (B31.3 para 331, B31.1 para 132, as I recall), but this audit did not confirm those numbers for current editions, so write 'verify clause/edition' for PWHT and welder ID. Don't let the 341/136 ref imply it covers them.

fieldReview.issue: There is no check for re-verifying earlier punch items or NCRs on the line. The user said most work at this stage is punch lists and confirming fixes are really done. That is the main reason for a repeat walkdown, and the checklist leaves it out.
fieldReview.fix: Add first in the 'Records (pre-walk)' group: {id:'prior_punch_closed', text:'Previous punch/NCR items closed, verified', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Punch closed, not fixed','Punch item still open','Fix caused new defect','Open NCR on line','Closure not signed'], unknownQuestion:'Where is the current punch/NCR list for this line, and who signs closure?'}

fieldReview.issue: Nothing covers the state of the line after its pressure test. Lines handed over late in construction often still hold test water, or have open ends and no preservation. Stainless demin lines and gas/air lines are especially at risk.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Temporary items' (or a new 'Preservation' group): {id:'post_test_preservation', text:'Drained/dried after test, ends sealed', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Test water not drained','Water at low point','Open end not sealed','N2 blanket lost','Preservation tag missing','Test water quality not recorded'], unknownQuestion:'What preservation applies after test (drain, dry, N2, inhibitor), and to which lines?'}. Add the same question to siteQuestions.

fieldReview.issue: siteQuestions asks which lines need flange bonding or earthing jumpers (e.g. fuel gas), but no check records the answer, so the walkdown can never log a missing jumper.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Finish & marking' (or a new 'Earthing' group): {id:'bonding_earthing', text:'Bonding jumpers/earth connections fitted', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Jumper missing','Jumper loose/corroded','Paint under earth lug','Earth boss missing','Insulating joint bridged'], unknownQuestion:'Which lines need flange bonding or earthing, and are insulating joints fitted?'}

fieldReview.issue: Expansion joints and bellows are missing. This includes rubber joints at pump suction and discharge on water systems. Shipping bars left in, wrong limit-rod settings and reversed flow liners are common handover punch items.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Supports': {id:'expansion_joints', text:'Expansion joints: shipping bars removed', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Shipping bar still fitted','Limit/tie rods not set','Bellows dented/damaged','Liner flow arrow reversed','Rubber joint cracked','Joint misaligned/overstretched'], unknownQuestion:'When are shipping bars removed, and what limit-rod settings does the vendor give?'}. The rod settings are vendor values, so they stay unknown.

fieldReview.issue: There are no spray shields on flanges of chemical dosing lines (acid, caustic, hypochlorite). This BOP-specific safety item can easily be a Category A punch.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Finish & marking' or 'Routing & condition': {id:'spray_shields', text:'Flange spray shields on chemical lines', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Spray shield missing','Shield loose/damaged','Shield wrong size/material'], unknownQuestion:'Which chemical lines require flange spray shields, and of what type?'}. Make the check N/A-able.

fieldReview.issue: The checklist assumes all piping is metallic. Water treatment, wastewater, raw water and chemical dosing commonly use GRE, HDPE, PVC/CPVC or lined steel, and these have their own defects: UV damage, point loads, over-tight clamps, and painted-over vent holes on PTFE-lined pipe.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Supports' (N/A-able): {id:'nonmetallic_lined', text:'Non-metallic/lined pipe: supports, UV, vents', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['UV protection missing','Point load, no pad/saddle','Clamp over-tightened','Pipe cracked/crazed','Lining vent hole painted over','Used as step/support'], unknownQuestion:'Which lines are non-metallic or lined, and what support/UV rules apply?'}

fieldReview.issue: Nothing checks where pipes pass through walls, floors or tank bunds (sleeve, seal, fire-stop). This is a common punch item that is easy to see on a walkdown.
fieldReview.fix: Add in 'Routing & condition': {id:'penetrations', text:'Wall/floor/bund sleeves sealed', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Sleeve missing','Seal/fire-stop missing','Pipe touching sleeve','Bund penetration leaking/open'], unknownQuestion:'Which penetrations need fire-stop or watertight seals, and to which detail?'}

fieldReview.issue: The 'Inline item reversed' defect is about orientation, not routing. The user's scope explicitly includes valve type and flow direction, but no check covers inline items (check valves, strainers, flow elements, steam traps).
fieldReview.fix: Remove 'Inline item reversed' from routing. Unless a separate valve/inline-item family already covers this, add {id:'inline_items', group:'Routing & condition', text:'Inline items fitted, flow direction right', basis:'project', codeRef:'', refConfidence:'none', defects:['Inline item missing','Flow direction reversed','Wrong valve type','Strainer basket missing','Not accessible for maintenance'], unknownQuestion:'Is a valve/inline-item list per line available for the walkdown?'}

fieldReview.issue: The 'Travel stop still fitted' defect assumes the stops should already be out. At handover to commissioning they are often kept in on purpose until before hot commissioning, and the draft's own unknownQuestion admits the timing is unknown. 'checked' in the text is not a pass condition. Common defects are also missing.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Spring hangers: stops/setting per plan'. Defects: replace 'Travel stop still fitted' with 'Stop status not tracked'. Keep 'Stop removed too early', 'Indicator off cold setting', 'Nameplate missing' and 'Rod/turnbuckle loose'. Add 'Hanger topped/bottomed out' and 'Rod out of vertical'. Keep the unknownQuestion, and add that the cold settings and rod-angle limits are vendor/project values (unknown).

fieldReview.issue: The text assumes every blind is removed. At system handover, boundary and isolation blinds or spectacles may stay in on purpose according to the commissioning status. 'Temp gasket left in' duplicates reinstatement. Temporary commissioning strainers and boundary isolation are missing.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Blinds per status list, temp items gone'. Defects: 'Test blind not removed', 'Spectacle not as status list', 'Blind not tagged/registered', 'Temp strainer not registered', 'Boundary isolation missing', 'Debris/scaffold left on line'. Move 'Temp gasket left in' to reinstatement only. Move 'Open end not capped' to post_test_preservation.

fieldReview.issue: Re-made joints are not checked for torque or a new gasket, although the user explicitly tracks whether torque was done and recorded. Some removed items (orifice plates, PSVs) may stay out on purpose until commissioning finishes flushing, so the defects should be checked against the register. 'Temp spool still fitted' is also listed under flush_record.
fieldReview.fix: Defects: 'Temp spool still fitted', 'Item not reinstated, not listed', 'Temp gasket not replaced', 'Gasket reused', 'Joint not torqued/recorded'. Drop the separate 'Instrument/PSV/Orifice' picks, or keep them only together with the 'not listed' wording. Remove 'Temp flushing spool left' from flush_record.

fieldReview.issue: 'no pockets' is wrong as a blanket rule. Designed pockets are acceptable when they have low-point drains, and liquid-full water lines often need no slope. As a defect, 'Pocket in line' would raise false punch items.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Slope per design, low points drained'. Defects: 'Slope reversed', 'Undrained low point', 'Pocket not on design', 'Sagging between supports'. Keep basis project and the existing unknownQuestion.

fieldReview.issue: The text 'valved and capped' assumes a closure arrangement (single valve plus cap). That is a project value; some ends are plugged or blinded, and others need double valves. Temporary hydrotest vents and drains, and drains routed to the wrong drain system (oily, chemical or clean) in BOP wastewater, are missing.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Drains/vents fitted, closed per spec'. Add defects: 'Temp test vent not removed', 'Single valve, double needed', 'Drain to wrong drain system'. Expand the unknownQuestion to: 'Which end closure (plug/cap/blind) and single or double valve are required?'

fieldReview.issue: 'Branch vibrating' cannot be seen on a pre-commissioning walkdown because the system is not running. 'Gusset missing' repeats 'Bracing missing'. Seal-weld and heavy-valve items are missing.
fieldReview.fix: Defects: 'Small-bore unsupported', 'Bracing missing', 'Heavy valve unsupported', 'Branch near pump unbraced', 'Seal weld missing (if spec)'. Add to the unknownQuestion: 'and are threaded joints to be seal-welded?'

fieldReview.issue: 'Debris at low point' cannot be seen from outside on a walkdown. 'Not in flushing scope' is a status, not a defect. 'Temp flushing spool left' duplicates reinstatement.
fieldReview.fix: Defects: 'Flushing not recorded', 'Acceptance not signed', 'Section missed in flush', 'Temp strainer status unclear'. Move 'Not in flushing scope' to an N/A choice. Delete 'Temp flushing spool left' (it stays under reinstatement).

fieldReview.issue: 'Line outside test limits' can be read as pressure limits as well as the test boundary. Welding on the pipe after the test is the most common post-test violation you can see on site (new support lugs or trunnions), and there is no pick for it. The gauge-calibration pick for record review is also missing.
fieldReview.fix: Defects: 'Test record not available', 'Test record not signed', 'Line not in a test boundary', 'Weld added after test', 'Modified after test, no retest', 'Gauge calibration not recorded', 'Joints insulated before test'.

fieldReview.issue: The unknownQuestion is empty. Gas and air lines in BOP (fuel gas, compressed air) that were hydrotested often had temporary supports added for the water weight, and without a list those supports are easy to miss.
fieldReview.fix: unknownQuestion: 'Were temporary supports added for hydrotest, and are they listed?' Add the same question to siteQuestions.

fieldReview.issue: The defects cover only loose U-bolts. A U-bolt that is double-nutted tight on a guided or sliding line is just as common, and it blocks thermal movement. Damaged supports and missing stainless-to-carbon-steel isolation (demin water lines) are also missing.
fieldReview.fix: Add defects: 'U-bolt tight on sliding line', 'Support bent/damaged', 'SS pipe on bare CS support'. Add an unknownQuestion clause: 'Is an isolation pad required between SS pipe and CS supports?'

fieldReview.issue: There is no check that the area where a temporary lug was removed has been ground flush and examined. This is the follow-up to 'Temp lug not removed'. Contamination of stainless pipe by carbon steel (rust staining from nearby grinding) is a common late-stage defect on demin lines.
fieldReview.fix: Add defects: 'Lug area not ground/examined', 'CS contamination on SS'. Add to the unknownQuestion: 'What examination is required after temporary lug removal?' (project, unknown).

fieldReview.issue: 'Wrong colour/system' cannot be confirmed on a walkdown: colour can be seen, but the coating system cannot. The soil-to-air transition of buried lines (fire water, raw water), a classic coating defect, is missing. The check also wrongly applies to unpainted stainless or non-metallic lines.
fieldReview.fix: Replace 'Wrong colour/system' with 'Wrong colour/colour band'. Add 'Wrap missing at grade entry'. Make the check N/A-able for unpainted SS and non-metallic lines. Keep DFT and the coating system as unknown (project).

fieldReview.issue: The main CUI defect (cladding overlaps that do not shed water) and insulation covering tags, nameplates or test points are missing.
fieldReview.fix: Add defects: 'Overlap not shedding water', 'Tag/nameplate covered', 'Insulation wet'.

fieldReview.issue: There is no PMI record pick, although stainless or alloy lines in demin water and chemical service usually need PMI under the project spec. PWHT is rare on BOP lines, so as an unconditional pick it is misleading.
fieldReview.fix: Add 'PMI record missing (alloy)'. Change 'PWHT record missing' to 'PWHT record missing (if req.)'. Add to the unknownQuestion: 'and is PMI required for this material?'

fieldReview.issue: Low pipes at walkways that are not marked as a head hazard are a common safety punch item on BOP walkdowns, and there is no pick for them.
fieldReview.fix: Add defect 'Low pipe at walkway unmarked'. Add to the unknownQuestion: 'and the minimum headroom over walkways?' (project, unknown).

fieldReview.issue: Several checks do not apply to every line (spring hangers, insulation, paint, small bore, expansion joints, spray shields, non-metallic). With only OK, OK with comments and Rejected available, an inspector would have to mark something OK that was never present, and that misstates the record.
fieldReview.fix: Add an 'applicable' flag per check, with an N/A tap kept separate from the three-level result. Exclude N/A checks from the line's overall result, and list them as N/A in the export.

fieldReview.issue: The new checks have no matching site questions. The blind and spectacle status at handover is also never asked about, although the test_blinds and reinstatement judgements depend on it.
fieldReview.fix: Append: 'Is there a blind/spectacle status list for handover, and who maintains it?'; 'What preservation applies after test, and to which lines?'; 'Were temporary hydrotest supports used, and are they listed?'; 'When are expansion-joint shipping bars removed?'; 'Which chemical lines need flange spray shields?'; 'Which lines are non-metallic or lined, and what support/UV rules apply?'; 'Which penetrations need fire-stop or watertight seals?'; 'Where is the current punch/NCR list for each line, and who signs closure?'

checks.text: Even gap, studs square, no visible strain
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class - verify clause/edition
defects: Studs not square / nut not flat
checks.unknownQuestion: Which alignment tolerance applies: the project spec or the value in the code edition?
checks.reasoning: The code requires alignment at assembly, but the clause, wording and tolerance change between editions (verify). A measured tolerance applies only at make-up or re-make. On a bolted joint, judge the visible evidence.

checks.text: Flange class/facing match mating flange
checks.codeRef: ASME B16.5 (NPS <= 24) / other standards per project - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: What rating and facing (RF/FF/RTJ) does the line class require, and what is the rule for mating with FF equipment nozzles?
checks.reasoning: The required rating and facing come from the project line class, which is unknown. B16.5 covers only NPS 1/2 to 24, so other flange standards may apply. A class or facing mismatch is a common walkdown finding.

checks.text: Pump/equipment nozzle: no pipe strain
checks.codeRef: API RP 686 (if adopted by project) - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: Is a free-bolting/pipe-strain check required at pump nozzles, who witnesses it, and must it come before final alignment?
checks.reasoning: Inferred from normal practice, not confirmed for this project. Piping forced onto a nozzle spoils the pump alignment. The signs are visible on a walkdown; the free-bolting check itself is normally witnessed and recorded.

checks.text: Gasket marking/colour per line class
checks.codeRef: ASME B16.20 colour coding - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: Which gasket type, material and inner/outer rings does each line class require?
checks.reasoning: Gasket selection comes from the project piping class. On a closed joint only the spiral-wound ring colour/stamp or the print on a sheet gasket's edge is visible. The inner ring and material can be fully checked only at make-up or re-make.

checks.text: Single gasket only
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 - verify clause/edition; ASME B31.3 para 335.2.4 (confirm project edition)
checks.reasoning: B31.3 para 335.2.4 allows no more than one gasket between contact faces (B31.3 lines). The B31.1 equivalent is not confirmed. Which code governs each line is a project question.

checks.text: Gasket centred, visible edge sound
checks.unknownQuestion: Are gasket sealants or compounds allowed by the project or gasket maker?
checks.reasoning: Practice checks, kept apart from the code item. On a closed joint only the outer edge is visible; protrusion into the bore can be seen only with the joint open.

checks.text: All holes bolted, correct size; washers if spec
checks.codeRef: ASME B16.5 (NPS 1/2-24) - verify clause/edition; other flanges per project standard
checks.unknownQuestion: Which flange standards apply besides B16.5 (e.g. B16.47, AWWA, EN, equipment nozzles), and are washers required?
checks.reasoning: The flange standard tables set bolt number and size (B16.5 covers NPS 1/2-24 only). Washers depend on the project bolting spec, so they are marked 'if spec'. A missing or undersize bolt is a pressure-boundary defect.

checks.text: Stud/nut grade marks match line class
checks.codeRef: Bolting material spec per project line class (e.g. ASTM A193/A194 if specified) - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: Which stud/nut grade and coating does each line class require?
checks.reasoning: The bolting material comes from the project line class. Which standard applies (A193/A194, A320, A453 or another) is unknown. Grade marks let you check in the field without paperwork.

checks.text: Studs fully through nuts, both ends
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 - verify clause/edition; ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 Bolt Length, wording differs by edition (confirm project edition)
checks.unknownQuestion: For B31.3 and B31.1 lines under the project editions/spec: is full engagement required or is one thread short allowed? Is there a min/max stud protrusion?
checks.reasoning: B31.3 para 335.2.3 (Bolt Length) covers nut engagement. Older editions allow one thread short; a later quoted version requires full engagement over the whole nut depth, so confirm the edition. B31.1: verify. Limits on excess or uneven projection come from the project, not the code.

checks.text: Bolts free of rust/damage, coating OK
checks.unknownQuestion: What is the rust acceptance (clean or replace), and what bolt protection is required (coating/grease/caps)?
checks.reasoning: Rusted bolts are a common 'OK with comments' item, but no acceptance criterion was given. Plain studs mixed with coated ones usually mean the joint was re-made.

checks.text: Torque done, marked and recorded
checks.codeRef: ASME PCC-1 (guidance only, not mandatory) - verify clause/edition; record requirement per project
checks.unknownQuestion: Is a per-joint torque/tension record and tightening mark required? Which method and value source apply, and who signs (subcontractor/QC)?
checks.reasoning: Recent B31.3 editions refer to PCC-1 as guidance only (verify clause/edition); the B31.1 reference is unknown. The record, method, marking and sign-off are project requirements. A field mark links the joint to its record.

checks.text: Studs removable, tool access clear
checks.unknownQuestion: Is a minimum tool/tensioner clearance specified at flanged joints?
checks.reasoning: Practice item and a common walkdown punch: studs that cannot be withdrawn or re-tightened block future maintenance. No clearance value is known.

citationAudit.evidence: Para 335.2.4 (Gaskets) under 335.2 Flanged Joints says no more than one gasket shall be used between contact faces. I already knew this, and secondary copies of the B31.3 text agree (safteng.net reproduction of B31.3 para 335; Brainscape/SlideShare B31.3 study material). The clause covers only 'one gasket'. 'Centred, undamaged' is practice, as the reasoning already says. I found no B31.1 equivalent, so 'verify' is correct there. Which code applies to which BOP line is a project question, so the line-class note was added.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 (confirm project edition); B31.1 - verify clause/edition
citationAudit.correctedRef: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 Bolt Length (confirm project edition - wording differs between editions); B31.1 - verify clause/edition. Applies per project line class (B31.1 or B31.3).
citationAudit.evidence: The number 335.2.3 'Bolt Length' is confirmed by several secondary sources. The content depends on the edition. Older text reads: 'Bolts should extend completely through their nuts. Any which fail to do so are considered acceptably engaged if the lack of complete engagement is not more than one thread' (Brainscape flashcards, eng-tips quotes, SlideShare API 570 practice questions). A later reproduction (safteng.net) instead reads 'Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut', with no one-thread allowance. I could not confirm which edition made the change, and I could not fetch the official text. Keep the number, but the ref must say the acceptance wording is edition-dependent. A forum post quotes B31.1 para 108.5.1 ('Bolts and bolt studs shall extend completely through the nuts'). That is a single unverified secondary source, so B31.1 stays 'verify clause/edition'. Do not cite 108.5.1.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 / B31.1 - verify clause/edition

The wording of what must be aligned differs between quoted versions: gasket contact surfaces to each other vs. flange faces to the design plane. Leaving it as 'verify' is the right call under the user's rule. Do not insert a tolerance value as the acceptance criterion. Only a wording tweak to make code applicability a project question.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 (confirm project edition); B31.1 lines - verify clause/edition
citationAudit.correctedRef: B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class. B31.3: para 335.2.3 Bolt Length (confirm project edition). B31.1: verify clause/edition.
citationAudit.evidence: The clause number and its content are confirmed. B31.3 335.2.3 'Bolt Length' says that bolts should extend completely through their nuts, and that a bolt is acceptably engaged if it is short by no more than one thread. A B31.3 study-aid flashcard set (brainscape.com) and a B31.3 practice-question deck (slideshare) quote this, and it matches long-standing B31.3 text. Note that B31.3 says 'should', not 'shall'. For B31.1, secondary sources (an eng-tips thread, and 46 CFR 56.25-20(e), which the Cornell LII annotation says reproduces B31.1 108.5.1) point to para 108.5.1 with 'shall extend completely through'. That is not certain enough for the current B31.1 numbering, so keep 'verify clause/edition' for B31.1. Fix the wording: which code applies to a valve is a project line-class question, so the ref should not put B31.3 first. Separately, the draft's reasoning says the engagement tolerance 'differs between editions'. No source supports that, and the one-thread wording appears stable. That is an invented claim (see contentFindings).

The safteng.net article 'Stop Valves in Pressure Relief Piping (ASME B31.3)' covers the same paragraph. I could not fetch the verbatim subparagraph text, so the tool should not paraphrase the (a) to (c) conditions. 322.6.1 permits several conditions, and 'locked or sealed open' is only one of them, so the checkpoint should not imply that LO/CSO is the only compliant arrangement. fieldReview.issue: (a) Missing: reinstatement of PSVs after hydrotest or flushing. At this stage PSVs are often taken out, blinded, spooled or gagged for testing. A PSV left blinded or gagged is the most serious valve defect a walkdown can find, and the draft has no check for it.
fieldReview.fix: Add check id 'psv_reinstated', group 'Relief valves', text 'PSV refitted; test blind/gag removed' (36 chars), basis 'project', codeRef '', refConfidence 'none', scope 'inferred'. Move the defect 'Outlet blinded or capped' from psv_discharge to this check, so that it can be Rejected and is not just observed.

fieldReview.issue: (a) Missing: reinstatement of in-line valves after flushing. Control valves, check-valve internals and wafer valves are often removed for flushing and replaced with spools, and test joints are broken. Most of the closure verification at this stage is exactly this.
fieldReview.fix: Add check id 'reinstated', group 'Body & ends', text 'In-line valve refitted; flush spool removed' (43 chars), basis 'project', refConfidence 'none', scope 'inferred'. fieldReview.fix: Add check id 'psv_bellows_vent', group 'Relief valves', text 'Bellows PSV bonnet vent open, not plugged' (41 chars), basis 'project' (manufacturer IOM), codeRef '', refConfidence 'none', scope 'inferred'. fieldReview.issue: (a) Missing: PSV mounting attitude and lifting lever. Both can be seen on a walkdown, and neither falls under the 'observe only' items (those are only the set-pressure tag and the discharge routing).

fieldReview.fix: Either point valve end joints to the flange family's checks, or add check id 'end_gasket', group 'Body & ends', text 'End gasket per line class; no temp gasket' (41 chars), basis 'project', scope 'confirmed'. checks.text: Rack & support bases, anchors, grout complete
checks.unknownQuestion: Civil spec: what grout type, thread projection rule, and post-installed anchor type and edge distance apply?
checks.reasoning: Covers rack column bases and floor/wall support anchors. Loose or ungrouted bases let supports shift. Whether nuts are tight cannot be confirmed by eye, and the civil values are not known, so none are assumed.

checks.text: Rack/support steel complete, bolts & welds
checks.unknownQuestion: Structural spec: what bolt tightening method and record, and which welding standard, apply to support steel? Is rack earthing checked here or by electrical QC?

checks.text: Support type & location as per drawing
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class. B31.3 para 321 'Piping Support' (design section, heading only; confirm project edition). B31.1 equivalent - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: Is the walkdown against the latest approved support drawing revision, and is this line B31.1 or B31.3?
checks.reasoning: Wrong or missing supports overload flanges and nozzles. Para 321 states design intent only; acceptance is against the approved support drawing.

checks.text: Supports at equipment nozzles in place
checks.unknownQuestion: Does QC witness a pipe-strain/free-bolting check at pump nozzles, and on which checklist is it recorded?
checks.reasoning: This is where support defects turn into equipment damage. A missing or temporary support at a nozzle loads the pump, and it must be found before hot commissioning.

checks.text: Small-bore, vents, drains, impulse lines supported
checks.unknownQuestion: Is there a project small-bore support standard, and is impulse-line support piping or instrument QC scope?
checks.reasoning: These are frequent BOP punch items. Instrument and cable hookups added late often leave small-bore lines and tubing unsupported.

checks.text: Pipe bearing on support, no lift-off
checks.unknownQuestion: Are any supports designed with an intentional cold gap (e.g. on thermal lines)?
checks.reasoning: A support that does not bear shifts load to its neighbours and to equipment, and sag leaves undrained pockets. Some gaps are by design, so confirm before rejecting.

checks.text: Shoe on steel, offset & length per detail
checks.unknownQuestion: Are shoes cold-offset for thermal growth, and what offset is specified?
checks.reasoning: Shoes may be offset on purpose, so 'centred' is not assumed. A shoe tack-welded to the beam becomes an unplanned anchor. The offset and length come from support/stress design.

checks.text: Guides, stops & anchors as per detail
checks.unknownQuestion: What guide gap, stop gap and anchor weld/bolt details does the support detail specify?
checks.reasoning: Guides, stops and anchors decide where the line grows. A wrong gap, or a guide welded to the shoe, sends thermal load to equipment nozzles. The gap values are project data.

checks.text: Slide plate/PTFE intact, clean, can slide
checks.unknownQuestion: Which supports specify PTFE or other low-friction pads?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if not fitted. Common late-stage defects are paint, spatter, tack welds, or welding heat after the pad was fitted, any of which locks the support.

checks.text: Free path for thermal movement, no clash
checks.unknownQuestion: Which lines run hot, and in which direction should they move?
checks.reasoning: Blocked movement only shows up at hot commissioning. It is cheaper to find cold, especially where cable and instrument hookups were added late.

checks.text: U-bolt/clamp snug or gap, pads per detail
checks.unknownQuestion: Which U-bolts are snug and which gapped, are lock nuts required, and which lines need pads or continuous support (SS, plastic, lined)?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if not fitted. A U-bolt clamped tight on a sliding line becomes a restraint. Missing isolation causes dissimilar-metal corrosion or crushes plastic pipe. Both are project details.

checks.text: Expansion joint shipping bars status noted
checks.unknownQuestion: Are there expansion joints in this system, and at what stage, and by whom, are shipping bars removed?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if none fitted. Shipping bars are temporary restraints, like spring stops. 'Obs:' picks record status only and are not punch, because the correct stage for removal is unknown.

checks.text: Travel stops / locking pins status noted
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class - verify clause/edition
checks.unknownQuestion: When are stops removed, by whom, and is a QC witness required? Must they stay in during hydrotest/flush, or are temp supports used?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if there are no spring/constant hangers. Observation only: stops in is often the correct state now. The real defects are early or unrecorded removal. 'Obs:' picks are status notes, not punch.

checks.text: Nameplate vs schedule; indicator (stops out)
checks.unknownQuestion: What type, size, load and cold position does the hanger schedule give, and who records the cold setting?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if none fitted. Type the schedule values in locally; no tolerance is assumed. With stops in, the indicator shows the factory preset, so record the indicator as N/A until stops are out.

checks.text: Rod: lock nuts, thread engaged, angle per detail
checks.unknownQuestion: What rod angle or cold offset of hanger rods is allowed?
checks.reasoning: Conditional: N/A if no rod hangers. Missing lock nuts or part-engaged turnbuckles let the setting drift. Rods may be offset cold on purpose, so 'plumb' is not assumed.

checks.text: Welds on pipe sound; no unapproved attachments
checks.codeRef: ASME B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class; ASME Sec IX (welder/WPS qualification) - verify clause/edition
defects: New weld on pipe after test
checks.unknownQuestion: Do support welds on pressure pipe need NDE/PWHT? If pipe was welded after hydrotest, what retest/NDE is required, and who approves it?
checks.reasoning: Welds on pressure pipe come under the piping code, made by Sec IX-qualified welders (qualification is checked on records, not by eye). Brackets welded late to tested pipe may invalidate the pressure test.

checks.reasoning: Erection and hydrotest temporaries left in place restrain the line and hide real support problems. A frequent pre-handover punch item.

checks.reasoning: Site welding damages coatings, and unsealed cladding at shoes lets water in under the insulation, so corrosion starts at supports. The repair system comes from the project paint spec.

citationAudit.evidence: Confirmed: the ASME tables of contents for B31.3-2020 (https://www.asme.org/wwwasmeorg/media/Codes-Standards/Find-Codes/B31-3_Process-Piping-2020-ToC.pdf) and B31.3-2022 (https://www.asme.org/getmedia/2d6bec7b-1177-4ee1-82ea-e5d5a86abab7/B31-3_2022_ToC.pdf) both list para 321 as 'Piping Support'. Secondary sources (blog.epcland.com/?p=16870, epcland.com/piping-supports-in-oil-and-gas/) quote 321.1.1 as stating the design objectives: no excessive stress, no leakage at joints, no excess load on equipment, and no unintended disengagement of the pipe from its supports. So the number and the heading are correct. Three problems remain. (1) Para 321 sits in the design chapter. It sets design objectives and does not require supports to be installed as drawn; that comes from the project support drawings. It is only a pointer to the topic, not the acceptance basis. (2) The ref ties the check to B31.3 alone, but whether a given BOP line is B31.1 or B31.3 is a project question (line class / code-boundary list). The ref should start with 'B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class'. (3) I believe B31.1 covers supports in paras 120/121 but I did not confirm it from a source, so it stays 'verify clause/edition'. I did not verify sub-clauses 321.2/321.3/321.4 and they should not be cited.

fieldReview.issue: The text assumes the shoe should be 'centred', but the draft's own question admits shoes may be cold-offset on purpose, so that is a guessed criterion. 'Enough length for movement' cannot be judged on a walkdown without travel data, which is unknown. The list also lacks the most common shoe defect: a shoe tack-welded to the beam, which turns it into an unplanned anchor.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Shoe on steel, offset & length per detail' (41 chars). Defects: replace 'Shoe off-centre' with 'Offset not per detail'. Add 'Shoe welded to beam' and 'Shoe weld cracked / partial'. Keep 'Shoe near beam edge', 'Shoe not attached to pipe' and 'Shoe too low for insulation'. Keep the unknownQuestion as it is.

fieldReview.issue: 'Nuts tight' contradicts the guide-type U-bolts that need a gap, which the draft's own question raises. Inspectors following the text would accept a U-bolt clamped tight on a sliding line, or punch a correct gapped one. The 'Lock nut missing' pick assumes double nuts are required, which is unknown.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'U-bolt/clamp fitted, snug or gap per detail' (43 chars). Defects: 'U-bolt missing', 'Nut loose / missing', 'Tight on guided line', 'Gap where snug req'd', 'Lock nut missing (if req'd)', 'Bolt not fully through nut', 'U-bolt bent / cutting coating'.

fieldReview.issue: 'Plumb' is a guessed criterion. Rods on hot lines are often set at a cold offset so they hang vertical when hot, and the draft's question says the allowed angle is unknown. 'Rod out of plumb' would raise false punches. The common defect of a rod rubbing steel or insulation is also missing.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Rod: lock nuts, thread engaged, angle per detail' (48 chars). Defects: change 'Rod out of plumb' to 'Rod angle not per detail'. Add 'Rod touching steel / insulation' and 'No thread visible in turnbuckle'. Keep 'Lock nut missing', 'Rod bent' and 'Hanger tag missing'.

fieldReview.issue: While travel stops or locking pins are still in, the indicator sits at the factory preset. That reading says nothing about the cold setting, so recording it then is misleading. 'Load indicator' fits variable springs only; constant hangers show travel. 'Cold mark not marked' is redundant wording.
fieldReview.fix: Text: 'Hanger indicator position noted (stops out)' (43 chars). Add the note 'Record only after stops removed; with stops in, record N/A'. Defects: 'Indicator off cold mark', 'Spring at end of travel', 'No cold mark on scale', 'Indicator unreadable', 'Nameplate unreadable'. Basis stays project, with no tolerance.

fieldReview.issue: This is an observation item, but its picks are written as defects. At this stage 'Travel stop still fitted' is usually the correct state, so it would create false punch items. The real defects are stops removed too early, during hydrotest or flushing, when the spring cannot carry the water weight, and stops removed with no record.
fieldReview.fix: Split the picks into status values (not punch): 'Stops IN' and 'Stops OUT'. Defect picks: 'Stop removed before hydro/flush', 'Stop removed, not recorded', 'Locking pin missing / lost', 'Stop status not tagged'. Add unknownQuestion: 'Must stops stay in during hydrotest/flush of spring-supported lines, or are temp supports used?'

fieldReview.issue: Two different bases are mixed under basis 'code'. Welds onto pressure pipe fall under the piping code. Welds on support steel only fall under a structural welding standard the project has not named (unknown). Sec IX welder qualification cannot be seen on a walkdown; it is a records item. 'Weld not painted' repeats paint_finish. Common visual defects (crack, porosity, undersize) are missing.
fieldReview.fix: Split into two checks. (1) 'Welds on pipe complete, no visible defect' (41 chars): basis code, codeRef 'ASME B31.1/B31.3 - verify clause/edition', refConfidence verify; defects 'Crack', 'Undercut on pipe', 'Arc strike on pipe', 'Porosity', 'Weld incomplete'. (2) 'Support steel welds complete, no defect' (39 chars): basis project; defects 'Weld missing', 'Undersize (visual)', 'Crack', 'Spatter'; unknownQuestion 'Which structural welding standard applies to support steel?'. Move Sec IX to the records check as 'Welder ID traceable (if req'd)'. Drop 'Weld not painted'.

fieldReview.issue: Missing late-stage check: welds or attachments made on pipe after pressure test. Cable-tray brackets, instrument stands, scaffold clamps and late support changes get welded or tied to tested pipe. For welds this can make the hydrotest invalid, and it is a frequent problem where instrument and cable hookups go in late.
fieldReview.fix: Add check id 'no_unapproved_attach', group 'Welding', text 'No unapproved welds or attachments on pipe' (42 chars). Basis project, codeRef 'ASME B31.1/B31.3 - verify clause/edition', refConfidence verify. Defects: 'New weld on tested pipe', 'Bracket welded to pipe', 'Cable/tube tied to pipe', 'Scaffold clamped to pipe', 'Arc strike on pipe'. unknownQuestion: 'If pipe is welded after hydrotest, what retest/NDE does the project require, and who approves it?'

Defects: 'Small-bore unsupported', 'Valve hanging on small-bore', 'Impulse line unclipped', 'Drain/vent hits steel', 'Tube clamp missing'. unknownQuestion: 'Is there a project small-bore support standard, and is impulse-line support piping or instrument QC scope?'

fieldReview.issue: Missing check: expansion joints and bellows. Their shipping bars or tie-rods are a temporary restraint, like spring travel stops, and leaving them in or taking them out at the wrong time damages equipment. BOP cooling-water lines may have bellows; whether these lines do is unknown.
fieldReview.fix: Add check id 'exp_joint', group 'Shoes, guides & stops', text 'Expansion joint shipping bars status noted' (42 chars). citationAudit.evidence: No clause number is cited, so there is nothing to refute. API RP 686 exists. Its 2nd edition (Dec 2009) has chapters that include Foundations, Mounting Plate Grouting, Piping, Shaft Alignment and Lubrication Systems (catalogue listings at saiglobal and standards.ie; Scribd copy). The standards.ie listing shows the 2009 edition superseded as of June 2024 with an 'ERR 1 2025' child document, so the current edition is UNCONFIRMED, and 'verify edition' is required. API 686 is a Recommended Practice written for petroleum, chemical and gas facilities. It is not among the codes the user named and is binding only if the project spec invokes it (already asked in siteQuestions). The ref should state that condition. The torque, rust and lock-nut defects are practice/spec items, not attributed to a 686 clause.

fieldReview.issue: A walkdown cannot judge 'No pipe strain' by eye. Strain only shows on dial indicators at the coupling while nozzle flanges are bolted up or broken, which is a witnessed check. The defects 'Pipe forced into nozzle' and 'Pipe weight on nozzle' are also not visible. Two of the most common nozzle-area finds on BOP water pumps are missing: expansion-joint control rods or bellows shipping bars, and spring-support travel stops. The reasoning states as fact that 'the B31 codes prohibit forcing pipe'. That is not confirmed for B31.1, and the meta text 'no clause was confirmed online' should be removed. There is also a hidden trap: the piping-family flange alignment tolerance may get applied at machine nozzles, where the vendor or spec value is usually tighter. That value is unknown.
fieldReview.fix: Change text to 'Nozzle flanges aligned; pipe supported near pump' (48 chars). Keep 'Flange misaligned at nozzle', 'Support missing near pump' and 'Temporary support left in place'. Replace the two unobservable defects with 'Support not bearing (gap)', 'Exp. joint rods not set', 'Bellows shipping bars left' and 'Spring stop status unclear'. Move the strain test to alignment_record as the defect 'Pipe-strain check not recorded'. Reasoning: 'Inferred: B31.3/B31.1 contain alignment/distortion requirements - verify clause/edition; governing code per system unknown.' Add the unknown question: 'Flange alignment tolerance at machine nozzles: vendor or spec value? Spring stops and exp.-joint rods: set or released at handover?'

fieldReview.issue: 'Temp covers/blinds left' is buried in a paint/housekeeping check. A test blind or plywood shipping disc left between nozzle flanges dead-heads or starves the pump, which is an A-type risk. Lumping it with D-type cosmetic paint gives one blended result per check and hides it in the summary. The user listed 'test blinds removed' as its own general check.
fieldReview.fix: Remove 'Temp covers/blinds left' here and add a NEW check 'Test blinds and nozzle covers removed' (37 chars), basis project (blind register). Defects: 'Test blind/spade left in', 'Shipping cover between flanges', 'Blind removed - not in register', 'Spectacle position unverified'. Unknown question: 'Who keeps the blind register, and is removal signed off before handover?' Keep paint_housekeeping for paint, debris and temp material only.

fieldReview.issue: The checklist has anchor bolts (baseplate to foundation) but nothing on the pump and motor hold-down bolts (feet to baseplate), shims, jack bolts or dowels. A loose hold-down bolt or a rusty, oversized shim pack is one of the most common rotating-equipment punch items and directly undermines the alignment record.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Pump/motor hold-down bolts tight; shims OK' (42 chars), group Foundation, basis practice, codeRef '' (citation auditor to decide). Defects: 'Hold-down bolt loose', 'Bolt not fully through nut', 'Shim pack excessive', 'Shims rusty/not stainless', 'Jack bolts not per spec', 'Dowels not fitted (if spec)'. Unknown question: 'Shim material and max count, jack-bolt treatment and dowelling per vendor/spec?' Do not put a shim count or material in the checkpoint text, because that is unknown.

fieldReview.issue: The draft is missing the most damaging and most common 'shipping' item on pumps: cartridge mechanical-seal setting clips, plates or spacers. If they are not removed after final alignment, the seal is destroyed on the first rotation. This happens often because responsibility (construction, vendor or commissioning) is unclear.
fieldReview.fix: Add the defect 'Seal setting clips not removed'. Extend unknownQuestion to: 'Who removes transit locks and seal setting clips (construction, vendor or commissioning), and at what stage?' Add the same item to siteQuestions.

fieldReview.issue: There is no check on coupling status. At handover, couplings are often left disconnected (spacer out) for the motor solo run. A missing spacer, or loose coupling bolts after reassembly, is a frequent find and decides whether the alignment record still applies.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Coupling connected, or spacer-out logged' (40 chars), group Coupling and rotation, basis project. Defects: 'Spacer out - not logged', 'Coupling bolts loose', 'Spacer/parts not stored/tagged', 'Guard refitted over open hub'. Unknown question: 'Is the coupling left open for solo run, and who reconnects it and re-checks alignment?'

fieldReview.issue: Nothing tells the inspector to check isolation status first. At this stage, systems handed to commissioning may be energised and under a permit-to-work system. Opening a guard, touching a terminal box or rotating a shaft can then be unsafe or outside QC's authority. This is a precondition, not a defect list.
fieldReview.fix: Add a first check 'Status/isolation tag checked first' (34 chars), group Identification, basis project. Defects: 'No status/LOTO tag', 'Energised - no PTW visible', 'Guard off while energised'. Unknown question: 'Once a system is handed to commissioning, may QC open guards or covers, and who issues access/PTW?'

fieldReview.issue: The user's main work at this stage is verifying punch closures, but the checklist only finds new defects. Nothing prompts re-verification of earlier punch items on the same tag, and the realistic failure modes are missing: closed on paper but still present, or new damage caused by the rework.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Prior punch items re-verified closed' (36 chars), group Records, basis project. Defects: 'Closed on paper, still open', 'Closure not signed by constr.', 'No closure photo', 'New damage from rework'. The tool should link this check to the open punch items saved locally for that tag.

fieldReview.issue: One check covers four unrelated items across two machine types ('Fan/compr.: belt guard, inlet screen, PSV, traps'). One OK, OK-with-comments or Rejected result cannot say which part failed, and the abbreviation is hard to scan. Defects that matter are missing: PSV gag or test blind left after hydrotest (A-type), broken PSV seal, PSV outlet not directed safely, open enclosure panels. 'PSV tag/cert missing' mixes an observation with a document.
fieldReview.fix: Split into two checks. 'Fan: belt guard, inlet screen, flex joint' (41) with defects 'Belt guard missing/open', 'Inlet/bird screen missing', 'Flex connector torn/taut', 'Damper linkage loose', 'Belt tension not recorded'. 'Compressor/blower: PSV sealed and tagged' (40) with defects 'PSV gag/blind not removed', 'PSV seal broken', 'PSV tag missing', 'PSV outlet not to safe point', 'Auto drain/trap not piped', 'Enclosure panel open', 'Inlet filter missing'. Keep the PSV certificate in unknownQuestion as a records question.

fieldReview.issue: There is no applicability path. Seal plan, temp strainer, fan, compressor, dosing and vertical-pump items will not apply to many tags. With only OK, OK-with-comments and Rejected, the inspector must either mark them OK, which is false, or skip them, which leaves a gap in the export.
fieldReview.fix: Add a per-check 'N/A' toggle that is not a result value. Better still, add a subtype pick at the start (horizontal pump / vertical or sump pump / dosing pump / fan / compressor or blower) that hides irrelevant checks. The export should list N/A checks separately so they are not read as OK.

fieldReview.issue: Every check assumes a horizontal pump. BOP raw water, wastewater and sump service relies heavily on vertical and submersible pumps. Their key pre-handover risk is construction debris or formwork left in the wet pit or sump, plus missing intake screens, loose discharge-head bolts, and missing guide rails or lifting chains for submersibles.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Wet pit/sump clean; screens fitted' (34 chars), basis practice, applicable to the vertical/sump subtype. Defects: 'Debris/formwork in sump', 'Intake screen missing', 'Discharge head bolts loose', 'Guide rail/lift chain missing', 'Submersible cable unsupported', 'Level switch not fitted'. Unknown question: 'Who signs off sump cleanliness before first fill?'

fieldReview.issue: The single most common motor-hookup punch item is missing: unused cable entries left open or closed only with plastic transit plugs. For fuel-gas areas, Ex marking is also not covered by any defect, even though the question about it exists.
fieldReview.fix: Add defects 'Unused entry not blanked', 'Plastic transit plug left', 'Ex marking not visible'. Keep the Ex requirement as unknown (area classification). Keep this check as observation-only, with electrical QC owning acceptance.

fieldReview.issue: Nothing covers the local control or emergency stop station at the motor. A missing, unlabelled or blocked local stop next to rotating equipment is a common safety punch item at handover.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Local stop station fitted and tagged' (36 chars), group Instruments and electrical, basis project, observation only. Defects: 'Local stop station missing', 'Stop button not labelled', 'Station blocked/far from motor', 'Station tag missing', 'Station cover/gland open'. Unknown question: 'Does the design require a local stop station at each motor, and where?'

fieldReview.issue: 'Grade per schedule' cannot be observed, because oil grade is not visible in a sump. The only visible evidence is a lube tag on the fill point. If first fill is vendor or commissioning scope, 'Oil level low/not visible' is a status, not a defect, and would create false punch items. Common finds are missing: oil leaks at bearing seals and missing grease nipples or relief plugs on grease-lubricated motors.
fieldReview.fix: Change text to 'Lube: level visible, tag fitted, no leaks' (41 chars). Replace 'Lube grade not identified' with 'Lube tag/label missing'. Add 'Oil leak at bearing' and 'Grease nipple/plug missing'. Add a non-punch status option 'Not filled yet (per plan)', to be used only once the site question on first-fill responsibility has been answered.

fieldReview.fix: Remove both. Use 'Temp strainer not in register', 'Strainer flag/tab missing', 'Flag not tagged/numbered', 'Tab shows no flow direction'. Keep the unknown question on whether a strainer is required here.

fieldReview.issue: 'Voids under baseplate' is not visible. It needs a tap or sounding test, which may not be permitted or practical on a finished, painted baseplate, so a walkdown can only record it if tapping was done. Common visible defects are missing: unsealed grout edges, spalled foundation concrete, and fill or vent holes left open.

fieldReview.fix: Remove it from rotation_arrow. Add a Records check 'Motor solo-run/rotation record seen' (35 chars), basis project, with defects 'Solo-run record missing', 'Rotation not recorded', 'Record not signed'. Keep the existing question about which package holds it (mechanical completion or commissioning).

fieldReview.issue: Late-stage risk is missing: an alignment record made before later rework (pipe modification, motor removal, re-shimming) no longer reflects the machine. The pipe-strain test record also has no home.
fieldReview.fix: Add defects 'Record predates rework' and 'Pipe-strain check not recorded'. Keep all tolerances unknown (vendor/spec), as already drafted.

fieldReview.issue: The user listed chemical dosing as BOP scope, and dosing skids are mostly rotating equipment (metering pumps). None of the typical dosing-pump items is covered: relief valve and its return, pulsation damper, calibration column, chemical leaks or drip tray.
fieldReview.fix: Add check 'Dosing pump: relief, damper, cal. pot' (37 chars), basis project, applicable to the dosing subtype. Defects: 'Relief valve missing/not piped', 'Pulsation damper missing', 'Calibration column missing', 'Chemical leak at pump head', 'Drip tray/bund missing'. Unknown question: 'Which dosing skids are vendor packages, and what relief, damper and calibration items does the design show?'

The reasoning's 'likely Cat A' is labelled inferred, which is fine, but the tool should not pre-fill a punch category. The project's category for this case is an open site question.

fieldReview.fix: Add defects 'Nameplate missing' and 'Tag no. wrong/duplicate'.

fieldReview.fix: Add defects 'Gauge glass broken' and 'Gauge not at zero (idle)'.

fieldReview.fix: Add defect 'Gland leak-off not piped'. Allow N/A when the datasheet shows no seal-support plan (seal plan stays unknown until checked against the local datasheet copy).

Who issues PTW?' 'Spring stops and expansion-joint rods: set or released at handover?' 'Nozzle flange alignment tolerance at machines: vendor or spec?' 'Is first oil fill construction scope? If not, how is not-filled recorded?' 'Who signs off sump cleanliness before first fill?'

checks.reasoning: Applies to chemical and fuel tanks that have a bund; N/A for unbunded raw or fire water tanks. Inferred practice: a crack, an open penetration or an open drain defeats containment.

checks.reasoning: Applies to all items on foundations. Inferred: water trapped at the tank chime or under a skid base causes hidden bottom corrosion, and cracked grout weakens support.

checks.unknownQuestion: Are flexible connectors or bellows specified at any tank nozzle?
checks.reasoning: Applies to all connected nozzles. Inferred: forced fit-up is a common late punch. It gets worse after tank settlement, and GRP or HDPE nozzles crack under pipe load.

checks.reasoning: Applies to all items; PG/TG mainly to pressure vessels and skids. Cable and instrument hookups are user-listed; device types and records are set by the project.

citationAudit.originalRef: API 650 para 10.1 (nameplates; confirm project edition)
citationAudit.correctedRef: API 650 Section 10.1 Nameplates (API 650 tanks only; confirm project edition). For ASME vessels or vendor skid vessels: verify clause/edition
citationAudit.evidence: Secondary sources (eng-tips thread 402594, amarineblog 'API 650 storage tank nameplate requirements', Scribd copy of API 650) quote Section 10 'Marking', 10.1 'Nameplates'. 10.1.1 requires a nameplate like Figure 10-1 and gives minimum letter height and required content, and 10.1.3/10.1.4 cover the fabricator and erector names. I am confident in the clause number and its content. The fix is about scope: the checkpoint also covers pressure vessels and skids, and 10.1 does not apply to those. The ref must name its scope so it is not read as covering a vessel nameplate. 'Match datasheet' is a project or user check, not an API 650 requirement.

citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 (bolt length; B31.3 piping only; confirm project edition)
citationAudit.correctedRef: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 Bolt Length (applies only where the connecting piping is B31.3 per project line class; confirm project edition). B31.1 equivalent: verify clause/edition. Tank/vessel nozzle itself: verify clause/edition
citationAudit.evidence: 335.2.3 sits in B31.3 Chapter V (335 Assembly and Erection > 335.2 Flanged Joints > 335.2.3 Bolt Length). I am confident in the number. Secondary sources (eng-tips FAQ 1331, API 570 B31.3 practice questions) quote the text: bolts 'should' extend completely through their nuts, and a bolt that does not is 'considered acceptably engaged if the lack of complete engagement is not more than one thread'. One eng-tips FAQ wrongly calls this a B31.1 paragraph. B31.1 does not use the 335 numbering, so that label is a misattribution and the B31.1 clause stays 'verify'. Two problems with the draft. (1) The clause is 'should' plus a one-thread tolerance, so 'bolts through nut' as a hard pass/fail overstates the code. (2) Which code governs the piping at a tank or vessel nozzle is a project line-class question. In a power plant much BOP piping may be B31.1, so the B31.3 ref must be conditional.

citationAudit.originalRef: API 650 / ASME Sec VIII Div 1 / ASME Sec V - verify clause/edition (reasoning: 'The VIII-1 hydrotest paragraph is UG-99 (confirm the project edition)')
citationAudit.correctedRef: API 650 / ASME Sec VIII Div 1 - verify clause/edition. VIII-1 standard hydrostatic test: UG-99 (only if the vessel is built to VIII-1; confirm project edition). citationAudit.evidence: UG-99 'Standard Hydrostatic Test' is the long-standing VIII-1 paragraph and is still UG-99 in recent editions (2019/2021/2023). I am confident. 'Verify' is right for the API 650 hydrotest and settlement clauses, since the draft gives no number. Small correction: Sec V sets NDE methods, not which records the handover needs, so citing it for 'NDE records available' attributes the requirement to the wrong code. The user did not name Sec VIII among the project codes, so whether any vessel is VIII-1 at all is unknown (already in siteQuestions). UG-99 must stay conditional on that.

fieldReview.issue: The family covers API 650 tanks, ASME pressure vessels, skid vessels and plastic tanks, but nothing filters checks by item type and there is no N/A option. Many checks do not apply to some items: a PSV on an atmospheric tank, a PVRV or flame arrestor on a pressure vessel, a bund on a raw or fire water tank, anchor bolts on an unanchored tank, box-up on a vessel that is already closed. With no N/A, the inspector must either mark OK falsely or raise a punch that is not real.
fieldReview.fix: Add appliesTo to each check (tank | pressure_vessel | skid | nonmetallic | chemical_service | insulated). The inspector picks the item type once when starting an item, and the list is filtered to match. Add a per-checkpoint 'N/A' option, kept separate from the item result (OK / OK with comments / Rejected). The export should list N/A checkpoints so a reviewer can challenge them.

fieldReview.issue: The text 'nuts tight' is wrong for the sliding saddle of a horizontal vessel (for example an air receiver or a fuel-gas KO drum or filter separator) and for some skid feet. Those nuts are set with a design gap or snug, not tight. Fully tightening them is itself a defect: it blocks thermal movement and loads the nozzles. The draft also assumes every tank is anchored, which is unknown for small API 650 tanks.
fieldReview.fix: Change the text to 'Anchor bolts: nuts fitted, full engagement' (42 chars). Add a check sliding_saddle: text 'Sliding saddle: slots clear, nuts per design' (43), basis project. Defects: 'Slide nut fully tightened', 'Slot blocked by grout/weld', 'Slide plate missing/painted', 'Saddle welded to base'. unknownQuestion: 'Which saddle is sliding, and what nut setting is specified (snug, gap, double nut)?' Add to the anchor_bolts unknownQuestion: 'Is this tank anchored at all per design?'

fieldReview.issue: There is no check for pipe strain or support at tank and vessel nozzles. Piping forced onto a nozzle is one of the most common late-construction punch items. It matters more on API 650 tanks after hydrotest settlement and on GRP/HDPE chemical tanks, whose nozzles crack under pipe load.
fieldReview.fix: Add check nozzle_pipe_strain, group 'Nozzles & manways'. Text: 'No pipe strain on nozzles; first support fitted' (46). Basis: practice. Defects: 'Pipe forced into nozzle', 'Flange gap/offset at nozzle', 'First support missing', 'Temp support at nozzle', 'Pipe weight on plastic nozzle'. unknownQuestion: 'Are flexible connectors or bellows specified at any tank nozzle?'

fieldReview.issue: Non-metallic tanks are missing. Chemical dosing, hypochlorite and some water-treatment tanks on BOP are often GRP/FRP or HDPE, not API 650 steel. Their typical walkdown defects (cracks at nozzles, UV degradation, loose hold-downs, unsupported nozzles, uneven base support) are not covered. The nameplate check's API 650 basis does not apply to them either.
fieldReview.fix: Add check nonmetallic_shell, group 'Shell & ID', appliesTo nonmetallic. Text: 'GRP/HDPE tank: no cracks, UV or chem damage' (43). Basis: practice. Defects: 'Crack/craze at nozzle', 'UV chalking/discolour', 'Hold-down strap loose', 'Base not fully supported', 'Weeping at seam'. unknownQuestion: 'Which tanks are GRP, HDPE or lined steel, and to what design standard (verify clause/edition)?'

fieldReview.issue: Shipping and transport restraints are not checked. Vendor skids and skid-mounted vessels arrive with transport brackets, shipping bolts and lifting beams. Leaving them in place is a common pre-commissioning A or B punch because they can damage equipment at start-up. temp_attachments only covers erection cleats.
fieldReview.fix: Add check shipping_restraints, group 'Shell & ID', appliesTo skid and pressure_vessel. Text: 'Shipping braces & transport stops removed' (41). Basis: practice. Defects: 'Transport bracket left on', 'Shipping bolt not removed', 'Marked shipping stop left in', 'Lifting beam left on skid'. unknownQuestion: 'Which restraints does the vendor mark for removal before start-up?'

fieldReview.issue: Preservation is asked about in siteQuestions but has no checkpoint. At handover, many vessels and skids sit for weeks under preservation (nitrogen blanket, desiccant, nozzle covers, drained after hydrotest). Lost preservation is a standard walkdown punch item.
fieldReview.fix: Add check preservation, group 'Records' or a new group 'Preservation'. Text: 'Preservation intact: covers, N2, dry' (36). Basis: project. Defects: 'Nozzle cover missing', 'N2 blanket pressure lost', 'Water left after hydrotest', 'Desiccant spent/missing', 'Preservation log not updated'. unknownQuestion: 'What preservation does the spec or vendor require for this item until commissioning?' Note that 'Plastic cap only' in blinds_spares may be acceptable as preservation on nozzles still waiting for piping. Make that pick apply to spare nozzles only.

fieldReview.issue: The user listed labelling under General, but no check covers content or hazard labelling on tanks. Acid, caustic, hypochlorite and fuel tanks need content and hazard signs. nameplate_tag covers only the equipment tag.
fieldReview.fix: Add check content_hazard_label, group 'Shell & ID'. Text: 'Content & hazard label fitted, legible' (38). Basis: project. Defects: 'Content label missing', 'Hazard sign missing', 'Wrong content shown', 'Label faded/painted over'. unknownQuestion: 'Which labelling and hazard-sign standard applies (client, local regulation or other)?'

fieldReview.issue: Flange spray guards on chemical-service nozzles are not covered. On acid, caustic and hypochlorite tank nozzles and manways, a missing spray guard is a common safety punch. Whether guards are required is set by the project, so this is unknown.

Defects: 'Spray guard missing', 'Guard wrong size/torn', 'Guard not secured'. unknownQuestion: 'Are flange spray guards required on chemical tank joints, and on which services?'

fieldReview.issue: Cathodic protection and insulation each appear only as a site question, or not at all, and neither has a checkpoint. If CP is fitted, a damaged or unlabelled test point is a real walkdown punch. Insulated vessels need checks on cladding and weatherproofing. The user listed insulation as a check item.
fieldReview.fix: Add check cp_test_point, appliesTo tank. Text: 'CP test point & cable intact, labelled' (38). Basis: project. Defects: 'Test box missing', 'CP cable damaged', 'Test point not labelled'. Add check insulation, appliesTo insulated. Text: 'Insulation/cladding complete, sealed' (36). Basis: project. Defects: 'Cladding open seam/gap', 'Insulation wet/damaged', 'Missing at nozzle/manway', 'Nameplate covered'. unknownQuestion: 'Which tanks or vessels are insulated, and for what purpose?'

fieldReview.issue: Local pressure and temperature gauges on pressure vessels (for example air receivers and fuel-gas skid vessels) are not covered. level_instruments covers level devices only.
fieldReview.fix: Add check local_gauges, group 'Instruments', appliesTo pressure_vessel and skid. Text: 'PG/TG fitted, valved, tagged, undamaged' (39). Basis: practice. Defects: 'Gauge missing', 'Gauge glass broken', 'No isolation valve', 'Gauge not tagged', 'Gauge unsupported'. The unknownQuestion contains a field check ('does the tag set pressure match the datasheet') rather than an unknown. fieldReview.issue: Basis 'code' with refConfidence 'sure' is applied to a mixed check. The nameplate requirement is code only for API 650 tanks. Tag fitting and datasheet match come from the project. Add the defect 'Code stamp missing (if req'd)'. (2) tag_datasheet: 'Tag & nameplate data match datasheet' (36), basis project. unknownQuestion: 'Which code is this item built to, and is a code stamp required on vessels?'

The quick-pick 'Bolt not fully through nut' may raise punches that the code accepts, since B31.3 treats a small shortfall in engagement as acceptable (verify clause/edition). Keep bolt engagement as basis code when the connecting piping is B31.3, otherwise practice. Change the pick to 'Bolt short of nut'. Add the unknownQuestion 'Does the project spec require bolt projection beyond the nut, stricter than code?' Add defects 'Gasket off-centre/protruding' and 'Mixed bolt grade/size'.

fieldReview.issue: This cannot be observed on most items at this stage, because most tanks and vessels are already boxed up. QC can only check the internals when the manway is open. Otherwise the check is a record check. As written, the inspector cannot honestly give a result.

The tell-tale basis is practice, with 'verify clause/edition' if a code basis is later wanted. 'DFT record missing' is a record, not something seen in the field: move it to test_records.

Questions raised by the new and revised checks are missing: whether each tank is anchored, sliding saddle settings, whether tanks are GRP or HDPE, flange spray guards, whether a code stamp is required, vendor shipping restraints, and labelling standard. Fixed fire protection on any fuel or hydrocarbon tank is not asked about at all.

checks.text: Root valve fitted, type/rating per hookup

checks.unknownQuestion: Which code (B31.1 or B31.3) governs this line, and what root valve type/rating does the hookup specify?
