checks.text: Small-bore tap braced, no heavy overhang
checks.unknownQuestion: Which taps must be braced on this project, and what bracing method is approved?
checks.reasoning: Inferred industry practice: a root valve and manifold hanging off a small tap on a vibrating line fails by fatigue. No clause is cited. The bracing rule and method are project items (unknown).

checks.text: Tie-in flange: bolts fully through nut
checks.codeRef: B31.1 bolt-length clause - verify clause/edition; ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 Bolt Length, acceptance wording differs by edition (confirm project edition)
checks.unknownQuestion: For the project code edition, is one thread short of full nut engagement acceptable?
checks.reasoning: Bolt-length wording differs between B31.3 editions: older text allowed one thread short, newer text requires full engagement through the nut depth. The project edition is unknown, so no tolerance is assumed. Mark N/A where the tie-in is not flanged.

checks.text: Tie-in: alignment, gasket, torque, threads
checks.unknownQuestion: What are the tie-in gasket type, torque record and alignment criteria, and are threaded connections seal-welded (on which services)?
checks.reasoning: Gasket, torque record, alignment acceptance and seal welding are project/spec items (not in 335.2.3), and their values are unknown. Bolt rust is a condition defect, not a code item.

checks.text: Impulse line slope & tap orientation per service
defects: Tap on top of liquid line
Tap at bottom of gas line
checks.unknownQuestion: Required slope value for this service (liquid, gas, steam)?
checks.reasoning: Direction is general practice (inferred): for liquid the instrument sits below the tap, for gas above, and steam uses condensate pots. A wrong slope traps gas or liquid. The slope value is a project item (unknown). Type any routing reference locally.

checks.text: Tube & fitting material/make per spec
checks.unknownQuestion: What tube material, OD/wall and fitting make does the spec require, and is mixing makes prohibited?
checks.reasoning: Mixed makes and wrong material are common causes of leaks. Wall thickness cannot be seen once installed, but OD and tube marking can. Correct values come only from the project spec (unknown).

checks.text: Compression fittings made up, no leak
checks.unknownQuestion: Which fitting maker's make-up/remake instructions apply, and is a gap-gauge record required?
checks.reasoning: The maker's make-up instructions are the usual acceptance basis (inferred), and a gap gauge is generally valid only for the first make-up. Whether a record is required is a project item. This check also applies to instrument-air tubing.

checks.text: Tubing/capillary supported, no strain or kink
checks.unknownQuestion: What are the max tubing support spacing, the isolator rule for SS on CS, and the capillary coil/support method?
checks.reasoning: Vibration, load and kinks cause fatigue leaks, and a crushed diaphragm-seal capillary means replacing the instrument (maker handling instructions, inferred). Spacing and isolator rules are project values (unknown).

checks.text: Vents/drains/test points fitted, ends plugged
checks.unknownQuestion: Which vents/drains/test points does the hookup show, and how should drains be routed on hazardous or hot service?
checks.reasoning: Plugging open ends is general safety practice (inferred), since an open end is a release risk when the line goes live. Which points are required is a project item. Valve position may be an intentional line-up, so record it as an observation only.

checks.text: Manifold fitted, HP/LP not reversed
checks.unknownQuestion: Which manifold type (2/3/5-valve) does the hookup specify?
checks.reasoning: Reversed HP/LP legs give a wrong DP or flow signal and are a common walkdown find. The equalizer position is set by the commissioning line-up, so record it as an observation only.

checks.text: Flow element/thermowell fitted, right way
checks.unknownQuestion: Are orifice plates, meters and TEs fitted now or after flushing, and what straight-run and earthing-ring requirements does the spec set?
checks.reasoning: Direction is read from the maker's arrow or tab marking (inferred). Reversed plates, spacers left in and plugged thermowell ports are common pre-commissioning finds. Straight-run length is a project value (unknown). N/A on other hookup types.

checks.text: Instrument/gauge rigid, intact, readable
checks.unknownQuestion: Which services need a siphon/snubber, are sunshades required, and are welded attachments allowed after the pressure test (is a retest needed)?
checks.reasoning: A loose mount causes vibration damage, and broken glass and overspray are routine late-construction punch items. A bracket welded to pressure pipe after the test may affect test validity; the rule is unknown (verify clause/edition).

checks.text: Tag fitted; nameplate matches datasheet
checks.unknownQuestion: What tag plate material and fixing does the project require, and which datasheet fields should be checked (range, material, rating)?
checks.reasoning: A wrong or missing tag blocks loop check and handover. The tag format and datasheet are project documents, checked locally.

checks.text: Glands tight & sealed; JB closed, labelled

checks.reasoning: Water and dust get in at glands and JB covers in site conditions. Gland type and rating depend on the project and area classification (unknown). Check the JB externally only unless scope and permit are confirmed.

checks.text: Cable supported in tray/conduit, protected
checks.unknownQuestion: What is the bend radius basis (maker or spec), which runs need covers, what IS/non-IS segregation rule applies, and what cable tag format is used?
checks.reasoning: Visual condition is general practice (inferred), and damaged or strained cables fail later. Bend radius, cover and segregation rules are project values (unknown), so no number is judged.

checks.text: Earthing/bonding fitted, lugs tight
checks.unknownQuestion: What instrument earthing scheme applies (PE vs IS/clean earth), at which end is the screen earthed, and what is the tray bonding rule?
checks.reasoning: Missing earthing is a safety risk. The governing earthing standard and scheme are unknown, so no clause is cited.

citationAudit.evidence: The paragraph number and title (335.2.3 Bolt Length) look right, but the draft's reasoning ('accepts a shortfall of up to one thread') matches only the OLDER wording ('Bolts should extend completely through their nuts. Any which fail to do so are considered acceptably engaged if the lack of complete engagement is not more than one thread'), which comes from a flashcard study aid and an Eng-Tips post. A newer reproduction on safteng.net reads 'Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut', with no one-thread allowance. From memory, this change came in about the 2016 edition, but I could not fetch the source to confirm the year. The project edition is unknown, so the acceptance criterion is unknown and the one-thread allowance must not be put into the tool. For B31.1, secondary sources (an Eng-Tips quote, and 46 CFR 56.25-20, which is said to reproduce B31.1) point to para 108.5.1 ('Bolts and bolt studs shall extend completely through the nuts'). I could not open the CFR text, so leave that as verify clause/edition and treat 108.5.1 only as a lead to check. Rust, gasket and torque record are not in 335.2.3; they are project/spec items. Sources: https://brainscape.com/flashcards/asme-b313-process-piping-3391803/packs/5002638 ; https://safteng.net/asme-b31-3-335-assembly-and-erection-of-flanged-joints/ ; https://www.eng-tips.com/viewthread.cfm?qid=116613 ; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-46/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-56/subpart-56.25/section-56.25-20

citationAudit.evidence: B31.1 122.3 is 'Instrument, Control, and Sampling Piping'. MSS SP-105 previews cite 'ASME B31.1, Article 122.3' as defining instrument valves, which confirms the number and topic. B31.3 322.3 'Instrument Piping' (under 322 Specific Piping Systems) matches my knowledge, but the search returned no quote of its text. The two problems: (1) the draft cites both codes together with a slash, which suggests both apply; which code governs which BOP system is a project question, so write 'B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class'. (2) refConfidence 'sure' overstates what the codes support. Neither paragraph sets root valve type or rating per hookup. B31.1 122.3 has a shutoff-valve-at-take-off requirement, but its sub-clause number and wording were not confirmed, and I am not sure B31.3 322.3 requires a block valve at all. Mark the confidence as 'sure - para number/scope only'. citationAudit.evidence: This is the only non-empty codeRef in the draft. It names a standard that exists: ANSI/ISEA Z358.1, the US standard for emergency eyewash and shower equipment (2014 edition, later reaffirmed). It cites no clause, paragraph or section number, so there is no number to disprove. It already carries the 'verify clause/edition' wording, and it already says applicability is a project question. That last point matters because Z358.1 is a US voluntary standard, and whether a Saudi project's HSE or design spec uses it is unknown. I did not search the web: there is no clause number to check, and I am not stating which edition is current. The existing 'verify edition' wording covers that. No change is needed. citationAudit.originalRef: ASME B31.3 para 341.3.3 (confirm project edition); B31.1 - verify clause/edition
citationAudit.correctedRef: B31.1 or B31.3 per project line class. If B31.3: para 341.3.3 (confirm project edition). If B31.1: verify clause/edition
citationAudit.evidence: Several secondary sources quote para 341.3.3 'Defective Components and Workmanship' across editions: an AWS forum thread (app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=92399), Eng-Tips threads (eng-tips.com/threads/asme-b31-3-nde.426991, /welding-lot.358239), and a progressive weld-sampling guide that says items are 'repaired or replaced & reexamined per 341.3.3' under 341.3.4. They all say repaired or replaced work must be re-examined with the original methods and acceptance criteria. I am confident the paragraph number is right. The wording does change by edition: a 2004-era quote has subpara (a), 'the repaired portion ... shall be examined ... same methods and acceptance criteria', and does not include 'to the same extent'. Later editions quoted on the AWS forum do include 'by the same methods, to the same extent, and by the same acceptance criteria'. Interpretation 22-04 (B31.3-2006) shows that the extent of re-examination after a repair (whole weld or repaired portion only) depends on whether the original examination was 100% or spot. Because of that, the reasoning should not quote exact wording as edition-independent. I did not confirm the B31.1 equivalent, so 'verify clause/edition' is correct for it. In a power plant, whether a line is B31.1 or B31.3 is a project line-class question, so the ref should say that explicitly rather than lead with B31.3.
